Recursively descend . and output each value.
Same as recurse without argument.

Examples:
> "a" | ..
"a"
> [1,2,3] | ..
[1,2,3]
1
2
3
> {"a":1,"b":{"c":3}} | ..
{"a":1,"b":{"c":3}}
1
{"c":3}
3
]

eval.tests.test_help_and_version.test_help_documented_function[empty-empty: Output nothing

Examples:
> empty
> [1,empty,2]
[1,2]
]

eval.tests.test_help_and_version.test_help_documented_function[length-length: Length of string, array, object, etc
- For string number of unicode codepoints
- For array number of elements in array
- For object number of key-value pairs
- For null zero
- For number the number itself
- For boolean is an error

Examples:
> [1,2,3] | length
3
> "abc" | length
3
> {"a":1,"b":2} | length
2
> null | length
0
> 123 | length
123
> true | length
error: length cannot be applied to: boolean (true)
]
